I dug into the current Desktop/agent architecture and I think this issue is pointing in the right direction, but it would help to tighten the implementation path a bit.

## What already exists

OpenCode already seems to have most of the hard infrastructure:

- PTY service in `packages/opencode/src/pty/*`
- PTY HTTP/WS routes in `packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/pty.ts`
- Desktop sidecar server in `packages/desktop-electron/src/main/server.ts`
- integrated terminal UI already backed by PTY

So the core problem does **not** look like “Desktop has no PTY support”.

The actual gap seems to be that the current agent shell execution path still goes through the one-shot non-interactive bash flow:

- `packages/opencode/src/tool/bash.ts`

That path is still fundamentally different from the integrated PTY terminal path, which explains why interactive flows like:

- `gh issue create --template`
- `sudo`
- `ssh`
- `vim`
- other stdin/TTY-dependent CLIs

still fail or degrade in Desktop.

## Suggested implementation direction

I would recommend **not** replacing the existing `bash` tool outright at first.

Instead, the safest path seems to be:

### Phase 1 — add an explicit PTY-backed tool
Introduce a new tool (for example `terminal`) with persistent PTY session support, something like:

- `create`
- `send`
- `read`
- `close`

This would let the agent opt into the PTY path only when true interactivity is needed.

### Phase 2 — wire it into Desktop UX
When the agent creates a PTY-backed session, Desktop should surface/focus that integrated terminal session so the user can observe or take over when needed.

### Phase 3 — keep `bash` for simple commands
Keep the existing `bash` path for non-interactive commands:

- `git status`
- `ls`
- `npm test`
- etc.

This avoids forcing PTY/session overhead on every shell call and lowers regression risk.

### Phase 4 — optional smart routing later
Only after the explicit PTY flow is stable, consider automatic heuristics for routing commands to PTY when they clearly require TTY behavior.

## Why this might be safer than a full bash replacement

This separates two very different execution modes:

1. **one-shot, output-oriented shell commands**
2. **stateful, interactive terminal sessions**

Trying to collapse both into one tool immediately may make the implementation harder to reason about and harder to review.

A separate PTY-backed tool gives:
- lower rollout risk
- clearer semantics
- easier testing
- easier fallback if something breaks

## Acceptance criteria I would use for this issue

I would consider this issue materially solved only if the agent can do all of the following through the PTY-backed path:

- create a PTY session
- send follow-up input to the same session
- read incremental output
- preserve shell state between calls
- close/cleanup the session reliably

And ideally verify against real cases like:

- `gh issue create --template`
- `sudo ...`
- `ssh ...`
- `vim` / `less`

## Bottom line

I agree with the direction of this issue.

My only refinement is:

> use the existing PTY infrastructure through an explicit terminal/session tool first, instead of immediately trying to replace all bash execution.

That seems like the cleanest and lowest-risk path to getting interactive Desktop agent workflows working.

Confirmed. The leak is scoped to `event.on(...)` calls inside components that remount on route navigation, not every call site.

Remount-scope leaks (3 call sites):

- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/routes/session/index.tsx:224` (`message.part.updated`)
- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/routes/session/index.tsx:254` (`session.status`)
- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/component/prompt/index.tsx:135` (`PromptAppend`)

Each `<Match>` flip in `app.tsx:862` (session route off and back on via home/plugin navigation) recreates the `<Session>` tree, including `<Prompt>`, and adds fresh listeners without disposing the prior ones. Session-to-session navigation within the same route keeps `<Session>` mounted, so that path does not leak.

Non-leak sites (run once at context/app init):

- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/app.tsx:742-784` (app root, mounted once)
- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/context/sync.tsx:114`, `context/project.tsx:64` (provider init, runs once)

`event.on` already returns `VoidFunction` via `@solid-primitives/event-bus` `EmitterOn`. `onCleanup` is the established idiom in this codebase (see `component/bg-pulse.tsx:32`, `component/dialog-theme-list.tsx:19`, `component/startup-loading.tsx:49`), and `plugin/runtime.ts:517` already uses `scope.track(api.event.on(type, handler))` which is the same pattern the three remount-scope sites are missing.

Minimal fix, applied to each of the three sites:

```tsx
onCleanup(event.on("message.part.updated", (evt) => { ... }))
```

Been exploring multiple alternatives, different approaches with a fork of OpenCode but also altering internal bits of git. None has felt very natural or ergonomic at all. So I'll close this issue for now.

Just for my own sake, here's some of the alternatives explored:
- Extending either the `info` type under messages or `parts` with a list of commit SHA's touched up that point (this includes reading git history, latest commit in current branch (or explored branches)  
- Putting a session id within the commit body (and which author it belongs to)
- Putting `relevant` parts of the transcription within commit body (a naive take on which parts should be relevant or not)
- Updating a git note with a OpenCode plugin on each commit made with OpenCode (and let OpenCode decide with a new session what should be relevant or not)
- Different takes on git commit hooks, both using bash, lua, python, OpenCode and even a dedicated application for injecting `relevant` information either in the commit body or as an attached note
- Modified git to support a separate index, which was designed to keep track on tools interacting with the repository. Contained tool version, commands ran and an output field. Was ran both as a pre and post commit hook (but invisible to the user)
